clue.text: Dish with fins chap cooked?

indicators.note: cooking turns raw ingredients into something new, so the letters are worked into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A meal made from a fish, fins and all, prepared by some bloke.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'Dish' does double duty: it is part of the letters to shuffle and, with the rest of the clue, the description of the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads as a playful description of Britain's classic battered fish served alongside fried potatoes.

clue.text: Following Grand Prix racing, girls at the finish certain to show cleavage

indicators.note: one thing following another means they come in sequence, so the later pieces are placed after the first

parts.note: Formula One (F1) is Grand Prix racing, with the digit read as the letter I

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: last letter of 'girls'
certain means sure

explanation.surface: After a motor race, the grid girls turn up in revealing outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: F1 becomes FI because the numeral 1 doubles for the letter I; FI + S + SURE gives FISSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleavage in geology is a splitting along planes, and a crack or split in rock is a fissure.

clue.text: After getting up, one's seat's designed for rests

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means rising from the bottom, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: one is I, plus the 's

indicators.note: something designed has been arranged into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Once someone has stood up, their chair turns out to be made for lounging.
explanation.walkthrough: I'S flipped upward gives SI; SEATS rearranged gives ESTAS, and together they make SIESTAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap taken in hot countries, so the plural is a set of short periods of sleep.

clue.text: Text marks lead-free waste hazards

indicators.note: free of its lead means without its leading letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: waste without its first letter
hazards are risks

explanation.surface: A written notice warns about the dangers of disposing of unleaded petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead-free' suggests unleaded fuel, but here it strips the first letter from the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Star-shaped typographic symbols used in printed writing to flag footnotes are called asterisks.

clue.text: Democrat standing gets knocked back

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
standing means status or rank

explanation.surface: A Democratic politician's poll standing suffers a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like a political reverse, but it is slang for swallowing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock back a drink is an informal idiom for swallowing it quickly, the past tense of drink.

clue.text: Push ecstasy hidden in drink, maybe bit of a laugh?

indicators.note: something concealed inside another thing sits within its outer letters

parts.note: to have a drink is one example of have, hence 'maybe'
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a single ho out of ho-ho-ho

explanation.surface: Slipping a pill into someone's drink might be thought of as a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink, maybe' works because drinking is one kind of having. The question mark also excuses taking a single syllable of laughter as a 'bit'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a sailors' cry while hauling, and giving someone the push is giving them the dismissal.

clue.text: Anticipate publicity with flipping Boris, e.g. wearing golf gear

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way round, so the letters read backwards
whatever is worn surrounds the wearer, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a tee is the peg a golf ball sits on
Boris Johnson was a Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Getting ahead of the press with a picture of a former leader in his golfing outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The flip covers the whole wrapped piece, not just the leader: reverse the golf gear with its contents after placing one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To pre-empt is to act first in expectation of something, forestalling it before it can happen.

clue.text: News outlet, European, that stands for transfer of power

definitions.text: that stands for transfer of power

parts.note: The Telegraph is a British newspaper
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A European media company champions the handing over of political control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stands for' sounds like advocating a political cause, but the thing literally stands upright; 'power' is electricity, not government. The Telegraph publishes this very puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall wooden posts along roads carry overhead wires that carry electricity and signals from place to place.

clue.text: Issue, to cross border, a railway pass in blue?

indicators.note: to cross something is to stretch over it from one side to the other, so the outer piece spans the rest

parts.note: to issue is to pour forth
a rim is a border
taken as written
RY is an abbreviation for railway
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A dispute about crossing the frontier with a train ticket, the pass perhaps printed in blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' is the verb meaning to flow out, split around the other four pieces. The question mark shows blue is just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is one of the three basic hues, alongside red and yellow, from which painters mix all others.

clue.text: Most natural energy displayed by 2 endlessly cycling

indicators.note: going round in a cycle moves a letter from one end to the other
without an end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
the answer to 2 down, without its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone with endless natural energy keeps pedalling round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: A bare number in a clue points to that entry's answer, here 2 down. Cycling moves the final letter round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: What comes most naturally to a person is what they find least difficult or effortful to do.

clue.text: Lay a carpet French way, back-to-front

parts.note: a mat is a small carpet

indicators.note: something back-to-front faces the opposite direction, so the letters read in reverse order

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: Instructions for fitting a rug the French way, oddly done in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like the verb for putting down carpet; it is the adjective meaning non-professional, as in a layman.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay people lack professional training, so a lay opinion is non-expert, just like one given by a hobbyist.

clue.text: Falsified quote involving a Republican hot line?

indicators.note: to involve something is to include it within, so the other letters take the extra ones inside
something falsified has been altered from the original, so these letters are changed in order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A doctored quotation from a Republican on a hotline suggests political scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R go into QUOTE, and the whole is rearranged. 'Hot line' looks like a telephone hotline; it is a line on the map where it is hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary circle round the Earth's middle runs through the tropics, where temperatures are consistently high.

clue.text: Shut up in tower by parent

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
a mum is a mother

explanation.surface: A child locked in a tower by their mother, fairy-tale style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' looks like being imprisoned; it is the command to stay silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay silent and reveal nothing is an informal British idiom for saying nothing about a secret.

clue.text: Grass changes story again, perhaps disowning it

definitions.note: a grass here as a plant type; the answer is plural

indicators.note: to disown something is to give it up, so those letters are removed

parts.note: one who revises a story again re-edits it; 'perhaps' because the story is just one example
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: An informer keeps changing their account, maybe denying it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' reads as a police informer, which fits the story-changing surface; it is the plant. REEDITS loses IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall water plants of the grass family, growing in marshes and at riversides.

clue.text: Advocate magnificent shipping harbour

indicators.note: to ship cargo is to take it on board, so one piece is carried inside another

parts.note: super means magnificent
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: A campaigner speaks up for a grand harbour busy with ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shipping' seems to describe a busy port, but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate is someone who publicly backs a cause, which is exactly what a backer or champion does.

clue.text: Sellers possibly accepting a pound limit

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the outer piece receives the inner

parts.note: Peter Sellers was a British comic actor; 'possibly' since he is one Peter
taken as written
to pound is to ram

explanation.surface: Traders might agree to a one-pound cap on prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sellers' looks like traders and 'pound' like money; Sellers is the actor Peter Sellers and pound is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A parameter is a boundary or set condition within which something must operate, hence a restriction.

clue.text: One teaching lacrosse for pupils nets on the counter

indicators.note: counter means running against, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
a net catches and holds things inside it, so the letters are held within the words

parts.note: the letters run through the middle of these words

explanation.surface: A school sports coach runs lacrosse and gets the pupils scoring goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nets' looks like goals in a lacrosse match and 'counter' like a counter-attack; the letters sit inside 'lacrosse for pupils' reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor is a senior academic whose job involves lecturing students at a university.

clue.text: Cube root botched after skipping university period

indicators.note: a botched job has been messed up, so the letters are jumbled
skipping something means leaving it out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A maths calculation goes wrong after a student skips a term at college.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove U from CUBE ROOT and rearrange the rest. 'Period' looks like a university term, but it is the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A month is a period of time, and the tenth month of the calendar year is this one.

clue.text: Retro style put away for spring

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: to style someone is to name them
to put away food is to eat it; past tense

explanation.surface: Vintage fashions are packed away to make room for the new season's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' is the verb meaning to give a title, and 'spring' is the verb meaning to arise, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring from a source is to arise or issue from it, as light or ideas flow outward.

clue.text: Kind of purple scrawl girl used regularly for reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run in reverse
something used at regular intervals is taken every other time, so alternate letters are kept

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A girl's purple-ink handwriting is reserved for writing thoughtful reflections.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters of 'scrawl girl' to get CALIL, then reverse it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale mauve shade named after the flowers of the lilac shrub.

clue.text: Hunger on the naval front — this killed many in the past

definitions.text: this killed many in the past

parts.note: to hunger for something is to long for it
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: Starvation among sailors in wartime was once a great killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunger' seems to be the killer; it gives the first half, and 'on' in a down clue puts it above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall medieval English weapon for shooting arrows was deadly at battles such as Agincourt.

clue.text: Nearly exploding about copyright theft

indicators.note: to be about something is to be around it, so one piece goes outside the other
an explosion blows things apart, so these letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
C is the copyright symbol

explanation.surface: Someone is almost livid about intellectual property being stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' is not trimming anything here; it is the letters to rearrange around C.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for stealing another person's goods, the crime of robbery.

clue.text: Difficulty of clue about season in Maine?

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a tip is a hint or clue
Americans call autumn fall; Maine is a US state

explanation.surface: A solver struggles with a clue about the weather in Maine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags Maine as just one American place where autumn is called fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden danger or snag, originally a concealed trap pit that animals fall into.

clue.text: Heads to Lowestoft after Yarmouth but yet to find place to stop

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only first letters are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A driver heading from Great Yarmouth to Lowestoft still hasn't found anywhere to pull over.
explanation.walkthrough: Lowestoft and Great Yarmouth are neighbouring towns on England's east coast. A lay-by is a roadside parking bay.
explanation.definitionFit: British roads have short pull-in bays beside the carriageway where drivers can park briefly and rest.

clue.text: Cross letters among religious houses

indicators.note: the answer is made of a run of letters already printed, not of meanings
to house something is to hold it within, so the words contain the answer

parts.note: the run of letters spanning these two words

explanation.surface: Angry letters circulate among monasteries and convents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry or the Christian symbol, which suits religious houses; it is a crossbreed. 'Among' looks like a link but holds the start of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel is a dog of mixed breeding, the result of crossing different types.

clue.text: Sign: recently evacuated, works shelved here

parts.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: an evacuated building has been emptied, so only the outside letters remain

parts.note: first and last letters of 'recently'

explanation.surface: A notice says the building was recently cleared and building works have been postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works shelved' reads as construction put on hold; the works are books on shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: A library is a building or room where books and other written works are stored on shelves for readers.

clue.text: Propose a meeting with universal representation

indicators.note: things meeting come together side by side, so the pieces are joined in sequence

parts.note: to table a motion is to propose it
taken as written
U is the film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: Someone suggests holding a meeting at which everyone is represented.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, to table a motion is to put it forward for discussion. U is the British film rating meaning suitable for all.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picture or staged scene that depicts something, so it is a portrayal.

clue.text: Little being revealed in eerie town near Gatwick when we take off east

parts.note: eerie means creepy

indicators.note: to take something off is to remove it, so that letter comes out

parts.note: Crawley is the West Sussex town beside Gatwick Airport
E is the abbreviation for east, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Something small shows up in a spooky town by the airport as our plane takes off eastward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests planes leaving Gatwick, London's second airport; here it removes E from CRAWLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal name for a small insect or spider is a creepy-crawly, a tiny creature that scuttles about.
